quote_text: I have held many things in my hands, and I have lost them all; but whatever I have placed in God's hands, that I still possess.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: Prayer is not overcoming God's reluctance, but laying hold of His willingness.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: Even if I knew that tomorrow the world would go to pieces, I would still plant my apple tree.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: Our Lord has written the promise of resurrection, not in books alone, but in every leaf in springtime.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: The body they may kill: God's truth abideth still; His kingdom is forever.
author: Martin Luther
source_title: A Mighty Fortress Is Our God

quote_text: A Christian is a perfectly free lord of all, subject to none. A Christian is a perfectly dutiful servant of all, subject to all.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: Faith is a living, daring confidence in God's grace, so sure and certain that a man could stake his life on it a thousand times.
author: Martin Luther

quote_text: Without knowledge of self there is no knowledge of God.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: A dog barks when his master is attacked. I would be a coward if I saw God's truth attacked and yet would remain silent.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: Nearly all wisdom we possess — true and sound wisdom — consists of two parts: the knowledge of God and of ourselves.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: We are not our own; therefore neither our reason nor our will should predominate in our deliberations and actions.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: God tolerates even our stammering, and pardons our ignorance whenever something inadvertently escapes us.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: To know God and yet to know nothing of our own misery, is of no use.
author: John Calvin

quote_text: As God delights in His own beauty, so must we learn to delight in His holiness.
author: Richard Sibbes

quote_text: There is more mercy in Christ than sin in us.
author: Richard Sibbes

quote_text: Christ's heart is open to us; it is always summer there, even when winter is abroad.
author: Richard Sibbes

quote_text: God will have us to look for and expect all things from him, because all good comes from him.
author: Richard Sibbes

quote_text: Christ in the house of affliction comes to the soul as an angel, with a coal from the altar.
author: Richard Sibbes

quote_text: Faith's greatest triumphs are achieved in the hour of deepest darkness.
author: Samuel Rutherford

quote_text: Christ is the very essence of all delights and pleasures, the very soul of all agreeable things.
author: Samuel Rutherford

quote_text: Grace tried is better than grace, and more than grace; it is glory in its infancy.
author: Samuel Rutherford

quote_text: Lay Christ's cross as a covering to keep the sun from you, that so the heat of affliction may not scorch you.
author: Samuel Rutherford

quote_text: How rich a debtor is he who owes his whole self to God!
author: Samuel Rutherford

quote_text: Take heed to yourselves, lest you be void of that saving grace of God which you offer to others.
author: Richard Baxter

quote_text: Spend your time in nothing which you know must be repented of; in nothing on which you might not pray for the blessing of God.
author: Richard Baxter

quote_text: God never forsakes his people but when they forsake him; and not until they have long and obstinately been forsaking him.
author: Richard Baxter

quote_text: If you are not praying fervently, you are not living at all as a Christian should live.
author: Richard Baxter

quote_text: Be killing sin, or sin will be killing you.
author: John Owen

quote_text: The vigor and power and comfort of our spiritual life depend on the mortification of the deeds of the flesh.
author: John Owen

quote_text: There is no death of sin without the death of Christ.
author: John Owen

quote_text: A man may be theologically knowing and spiritually ignorant.
author: John Owen

quote_text: He that learns to love God in all and above all things shall find rest everywhere, even in the midst of distractions.
author: John Owen

quote_text: Till sin be bitter, Christ will not be sweet.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: The way to be humble is to behold Christ's humility.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: When thou art at the worst, God is at the best.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: Love to God is the foundation of all duty.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: Faith and repentance are the two wings by which we fly to Christ.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: God will have us look upon trials as the medicines by which He purges our corruption.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: Man cannot cover what God would reveal.
author: Thomas Watson

quote_text: Prayer will make a man cease from sin, or sin will entice a man to cease from prayer.
author: John Bunyan

quote_text: In prayer it is better to have a heart without words than words without a heart.
author: John Bunyan

quote_text: It is an easy thing for those that are in the sunshine to tell them that walk in the dark to rejoice.
author: John Bunyan

quote_text: The jewel of the Christian is his conscience void of offence.
author: John Bunyan

quote_text: One leak will sink a ship; and one sin will destroy a sinner.
author: John Bunyan

quote_text: They who would have good wages must be careful to do good work.
author: Matthew Henry
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible

quote_text: Extraordinary afflictions are not always the punishment of extraordinary sins, but sometimes the trial of extraordinary graces.
author: Matthew Henry
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible

quote_text: It is folly to pretend to that which we have not, and wisdom to improve what we have.
author: Matthew Henry
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible

quote_text: He is able who is willing, and He is willing who is able; and He is both.
author: Matthew Henry
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible

quote_text: None so empty of grace as those that are full of themselves.
author: Matthew Henry
source_title: Matthew Henry's Commentary on the Whole Bible

quote_text: Receive every day as a resurrection from death, as a new enjoyment of life.
author: William Law
source_title: A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life

quote_text: There is nothing that makes us love a man so much as praying for him.
author: William Law
source_title: A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life

quote_text: The devout man prays not only for himself but for the whole world, for the poor, the rich, the sick, the sound, the young, and the old.
author: William Law
source_title: A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life

quote_text: The grace of God is not given to us for nothing; it is given that we may be holy.
author: William Law
source_title: A Serious Call to a Devout and Holy Life

quote_text: Though we cannot think alike, may we not love alike?
author: John Wesley

quote_text: I am no longer my own, but Thine. Put me to what Thou wilt, rank me with whom Thou wilt.
author: John Wesley
source_title: A Covenant Prayer in the Wesleyan Tradition

quote_text: Do all the good you can, by all the means you can, in all the ways you can, in all the places you can, at all the times you can, to all the people you can, as long as ever you can.
author: John Wesley

quote_text: Give me one hundred preachers who fear nothing but sin and desire nothing but God, and I care not whether they be clergymen or laymen, they alone will shake the gates of Hell.
author: John Wesley

quote_text: Go on, go on! Be not weary of well-doing. Greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.
author: John Wesley

quote_text: We are immortal till our work on earth is done.
author: George Whitefield

quote_text: God forbid that I should travel with anybody a quarter of an hour without speaking of Christ to them.
author: George Whitefield

quote_text: I had rather wear out than rust out.
author: George Whitefield

quote_text: Do good now; you have but a little time to live, a little time to do good.
author: George Whitefield

quote_text: Grace is but glory begun, and glory is but grace perfected.
author: Jonathan Edwards

quote_text: Resolved, never to do anything which I should be afraid to do if it were the last hour of my life.
author: Jonathan Edwards

quote_text: The enjoyment of God is the only happiness with which our souls can be satisfied.
author: Jonathan Edwards
source_title: The End for Which God Created the World

quote_text: God is glorified not only by His glory's being seen, but by its being rejoiced in.
author: Jonathan Edwards
source_title: The End for Which God Created the World

quote_text: The pleasures of this world are but shadows; but the pleasures at God's right hand are substantial.
author: Jonathan Edwards

quote_text: I claim no right to myself — no right to this understanding, this will, these affections that are in me; they are all God's.
author: Jonathan Edwards

quote_text: Sincerity makes the very least person to be of more value than the most talented hypocrite.
author: Jonathan Edwards

quote_text: I have a great need for Christ: I have a great Christ for my need.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: By perseverance the snail reached the ark.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: Discernment is not knowing the difference between right and wrong. It is knowing the difference between right and almost right.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: Anxiety does not empty tomorrow of its sorrows, but only empties today of its strength.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: Nobody ever outgrows Scripture; the book widens and deepens with our years.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: I have learned to kiss the wave that throws me against the Rock of Ages.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: No man can do me a truer kindness in this world than to pray for me.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: Faith goes up the stairs that love has built and looks out the windows which hope has opened.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: To be a soul winner is the greatest joy in the world.
author: Charles H. Spurgeon

quote_text: An ineffable but all-sufficient sacrifice had to be made before God could righteously forgive His people.
author: Arthur W. Pink

quote_text: Growth in grace is not the work of a day, nor a month, nor a year, but of a whole life.
author: Arthur W. Pink

quote_text: The soul that has felt the drawing of divine grace is never again satisfied with the things of earth.
author: Arthur W. Pink

quote_text: True salvation changes the whole man from the inside out.
author: Arthur W. Pink
